newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - COFFEE EXPECTED TO FALL, THREATENS SUPPORT.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - COFFEE EXPECTED TO FALL, THREATENS SUPPORT.

text.p: SEPT Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Robusta coffee futures are poised to challenge nearby support and target a breakaway gap which would signal a total retracement of this year's gains, technical analysts said on Thursday.
The London market was called to open unchanged to $20 lower than Wednesday's close.
"Coffee is about to take out an important low," said Trevor Neil, senior technical analyst at Union Cal Futures.

Fund and commission house rollovers amid a lack of roaster demand pressured the nearby September contract to a session low of $1,485 on Wednesday, forming a a double bottom with the $1,477 low scored on July 22.
"This will probably be broken today which will turn those points into resistance," Neil said, pegging the next level at $1,446.

A chart gap created in January between $1,368 and $1,415 should also act as a downside hurdle but once broken would signify that the market would have retraced most of the gains amassed since January.
"It looks as though we will revisit the breakaway gap which started the whole move this year," Neil said.
In fundamental news, the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell by 606 60-kg bags as of August 12, to 92,959 bags. There were an additional 5,853 bags of coffee pending grading.
The Brazilian Coffee Exporters' Association (Abecafe) quoted the Industry and Commerce Ministry as saying green coffee exports totalled 1.03 million 60-kg bags in July.

This was 12 percent down from the 1.18 million bags shipped in the same month last year but Abecafe said it was still anticipating total shipments in 1997 to reach 16.5 million bags, up 27 percent from 1996.
